paragraphs: LKQ Corporation ("LKQ," the "Company" or "we") is a global distributor of vehicle products, including replacement parts, components and systems used in the repair and maintenance of vehicles, and specialty aftermarket products and accessories to improve the performance, functionality and appearance of vehicles.

Buyers of vehicle replacement products have the option to purchase from primarily four sources: new products produced by original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs"); new products produced by companies other than the OEMs, which are referred to as aftermarket products; salvaged products taken from total loss vehicles; and reconditioned products that have been refurbished or remanufactured. Collectively, we refer to the three sources that are not new OEM products as alternative parts.

We sell a variety of alternative replacement and maintenance parts including collision parts, which are typically exterior components used in the collision repair process to restore a vehicle's appearance and safety, such as bumper covers, fenders, paint and related body repair products, and lights; hard parts, which are typically internal components that are either mechanical in nature, such as alternators, starters, and clutches, or functional components that are replaced as part of routine maintenance, such as brake pads, discs and sensors, filters and batteries; and major mechanical parts, such as engines and transmissions. We also sell specialty products and accessories, which are vehicle products that improve the performance, functionality and appearance of vehicles.

We are organized into three operating segments: North America (formerly known as ("f/k/a") Wholesale - North America); Europe; and Specialty, each of which is presented as a reportable segment. Refer to Note 12, "Revenue Recognition" and Note 26, "Segment and Geographic Information" to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for financial information by reportable segment and by geographic region.

Our North America segment is a leading provider of alternative vehicle collision replacement products, paint and related body repair products, and alternative vehicle mechanical replacement and maintenance products, with our sales, processing, and distribution facilities reaching most major markets in the United States ("U.S.") and Canada. Our Europe segment is a leading provider of alternative vehicle replacement and maintenance products in Germany, the United Kingdom ("U.K."), the Benelux region (Belgium, Netherlands, and Luxembourg), Italy, Czech Republic, Austria, Slovakia, France and various other European countries. Our Specialty segment is a leading distributor of specialty vehicle aftermarket products and accessories reaching most major markets in the U.S. and Canada.

On September 30, 2025, we completed the sale of our Self Service segment to an affiliate of Pacific Avenue Capital Partners, LLC. We have made certain reclassifications to the prior period financial information to reflect discontinued operations presentation as a result of the sale of our Self Service segment. Refer to Note 4, "Discontinued Operations and Divestitures" to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information.

Our mission is to be the leading global value-added and sustainable distributor of vehicle parts and accessories by offering our customers the most comprehensive, available and cost-effective selection of parts and service solutions while building strong partnerships with our employees and the communities in which we operate. To achieve this mission, our strategy focuses on executing three key initiatives:

We are dedicated to building competitive advantages, widening the moats around each of our operating segments, and maintaining our leadership positions in the markets in which we operate. We focus on profitable growth and increasing free cash flow while maintaining a resilient, investment grade balance sheet. We foster an entrepreneurial and employee-centric culture that enables agility and innovation, empowering our businesses to succeed in the markets they serve with a compensation structure that is aligned with our strategy to deliver long-term total shareholder returns. To continuously enhance the quality of our portfolio, our growth strategy is driven by organic investments in automation, productivity improvements, talent development, and strategic acquisitions that are aligned with the ongoing evolution of the car parc.

We are committed to generating sustainable returns on invested capital by driving operational excellence and lean management across our businesses. We continuously evaluate and pursue initiatives to improve operating efficiencies, enhance margins and leverage the intellectual capital opportunities that exist across our operating segments. Through targeted productivity efforts and a disciplined approach to cost management, we target specific performance metrics including free cash flow generation, organic growth and margins. Our current initiatives include optimizing working capital, enhancing margins through our inventory optimization efforts and reducing selling, general and administrative costs through streamlining our footprint and reducing complexity across our business.

We are focused on maximizing return on invested capital through an efficient capital allocation strategy. We apply strict criteria, targeting accretive tuck-in acquisitions with high synergies that align with the core businesses and strategy. We proactively divest businesses that no longer align with our strategic vision, financial objectives or have limited long-term value potential, as demonstrated by our divestments of certain operations in Poland, Slovenia, and Bosnia in 2024 and our Self Service segment in 2025. Additionally, in 2025, aligning with our ongoing strategy to simplify our portfolio and concentrate on our core segments, we commenced a process to explore the potential sale of our Specialty segment. Finally, we maintain a prudent and disciplined financial policy that prioritizes returning cash to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends, while maintaining our investment grade credit rating.

In addition to the above, on January 26, 2026 our Board of Directors (the "Board") announced it has initiated a comprehensive review of strategic alternatives to enhance shareholder value. As part of the review, the Board is working with its advisors to evaluate our strategic alternatives, including a potential sale of the Company.

As part of executing our strategy to deliver profitable growth, drive a lean operating model and maximize returns on invested capital, we will, from time to time, engage in restructuring and business transformation initiatives. These initiatives can range in scope from broad changes such as centralizing and standardizing non-customer facing teams and divesting non-strategic assets, to targeted changes such as, consolidating underutilized facilities and closing underperforming locations. Executing on these initiatives can take a few months to several years to fully implement depending on the scope and complexity of the initiative. Additionally, initiatives can change or expand based on the information obtained while executing on the initiative and when additional initiative activities are identified. See Note 13, "Restructuring and Transaction Related Expenses" to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information on restructuring charges related to these initiatives.

Our North America segment operates in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico. In the U.S. and Canada, we primarily sell aftermarket, salvage and reconditioned collision parts; aftermarket and salvage hard parts; and salvage and reconditioned major mechanical parts through our businesses, including Keystone and Bumper to Bumper (f/k/a Canadian Automotive Group), amongst others. We also, to a lesser extent, provide services for vehicles including mobile and remote diagnostics services and hybrid battery reconditioning and installation services through our businesses, including Elitek Vehicle Services and Green Bean Battery, amongst others. In Mexico, we remanufacture engines and transmissions for sale in the U.S.

Our aftermarket products encompass items commonly prone to damage in a collision, including bumper covers, fenders, paint and paint related body repair products, and lights, as well as mechanical automotive parts and accessories. Our private label products include the Platinum Plus line which is marketed under the Keystone brand and the "Value Line" product category designed for value‑oriented, often self‑pay, consumers. Certain products receive certifications from the Certified Automotive Parts Association, an independent organization that evaluates the quality and performance of aftermarket parts relative to OEM collision replacement products. Our salvage products include both mechanical and collision parts, including engines; transmissions; door assemblies; sheet metal products such as trunk lids, fenders and hoods; lights; and bumper assemblies.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business
We face competition from local, national, international, and internet-based vehicle products providers, and this competition could negatively affect our business.
We rely upon insurance companies and our customers to promote the usage of alternative parts.
Intellectual property claims relating to aftermarket products could adversely affect our business.
If the number of vehicles involved in accidents or being repaired declines, or the mix of the types of vehicles in the overall vehicle population changes, our business could suffer.
Fluctuations in the prices of commodities could adversely affect our financial results.
Future public health emergencies could have a material adverse impact on our business, results of operation, financial condition and liquidity, the nature and extent of which is highly uncertain.
If we determine that our goodwill or other intangible assets have become impaired, we may incur significant charges to our pretax income.
We could be subject to product liability claims and involved in product recalls.
We may not be able to successfully acquire businesses or integrate acquisitions, and we may not be able to successfully divest certain businesses.
Risks Relating to Our Financial Structure

We have a substantial amount of indebtedness, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and our ability to obtain financing in the future and to react to changes in our business.
Each of our credit agreement and CAD Note imposes operating and financial restrictions on us and our subsidiaries, which may prevent us from capitalizing on business opportunities.

We may not be able to generate sufficient cash to service all of our indebtedness and may be forced to take other actions to satisfy our obligations under our indebtedness, which may not be successful.
Our future capital needs may require that we seek to refinance our debt or obtain additional debt or equity financing, events that could have a negative effect on our business.
Our variable rate indebtedness subjects us to interest rate risk, which could cause our indebtedness service obligations to increase significantly.
Repayment of our indebtedness is dependent on cash flow generated by our subsidiaries.
A downgrade in our credit rating would impact us.
The amount and frequency of our share repurchases and dividend payments may fluctuate.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
We are subject to environmental regulations and incur costs relating to environmental matters.
We may be adversely affected by legal, regulatory or market responses to global climate change.
paragraphs: The following risk factors and other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K should be carefully considered. The occurrence of any of the following risks or of unknown risks and uncertainties may adversely affect our business, operating results and financial condition.

Our operating results and financial condition have been and could continue to be adversely affected by the economic, political and social conditions in North America, Europe, Taiwan and other countries, as well as the economic health of vehicle owners and numbers and types of vehicles sold.

Changes in economic, political and social conditions in North America, Europe, Taiwan and other countries in which we are located or do business could have a material effect on our company. Negative effects to our supply chain, costs of doing business, sales and distribution activity may occur due to factors such as war or threats of war, restrictive governmental actions (e.g., tariffs), natural disasters, nuclear facility accidents, public health emergencies, major logistics disruptions, sanctions, utility interruptions, terrorism and social unrest.

Our business is also affected by a number of other factors. For example, the number and types of new vehicles produced and sold by OEM affects our business. A decrease in the number of vehicles on the road may result in a decrease in repairs. In addition, our sales are impacted by changes to the economic health of vehicle owners. The economic health of vehicle owners is affected by many factors, including, among others, general business conditions, interest rates, inflation, insurance premiums and deductibles, consumer debt levels, the availability of consumer credit, taxation, fuel prices, new and used vehicle pricing, unemployment trends and other matters that influence consumer confidence and spending. Many of these factors are outside of our control. If inflationary pressures or any of these other conditions worsen, our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows could be adversely affected.

In addition, economic conditions, including decreased access to credit, may result in financial difficulties leading to restructurings, bankruptcies, liquidations and other unfavorable events for our customers, suppliers, logistics and other service providers and financial institutions that are counterparties to our credit facilities and hedge transactions. These unfavorable events affecting our business partners could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

We have a presence in Ukraine and are monitoring the situation there carefully. In addition, a number of our suppliers are based in China and Taiwan and so increasing strains and any political repercussions may have implications upon our supply chain.

paragraphs: The following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our audited Consolidated Financial Statements and notes thereto included in Part II, Item 8, "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data," of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Our operating results have fluctuated on a quarterly and annual basis in the past and can be expected to continue to fluctuate in the future as a result of a number of factors, some of which are beyond our control. Please refer to the factors referred to in the Special Note on Forward-Looking Statements and Risk Factors above. Accordingly, our historical results of operations may not be indicative of future performance.

We continuously manage and assess the businesses and investments we own and the markets in which we operate. Our acquisition strategy is to target highly accretive tuck-in acquisitions with significant synergies or critical capabilities. core segments, we commenced a process to explore the potential sale of our Specialty segment. As part of the review, the Board is working with its advisors to evaluate our strategic alternatives, including a potential sale of the Company.

We report our revenue in two categories: (i) parts and services and (ii) other. Our parts revenue is generated from the sale of alternative parts and vehicle products including collision parts, which are typically exterior components used in the collision repair process to restore a vehicle's appearance and safety; hard parts, which are typically internal components that are either mechanical in nature or functional components that are replaced as part of routine maintenance; major mechanical parts; and specialty products and accessories, which are vehicle products that improve the performance, functionality and appearance of vehicles. Services revenue includes additional services that are generally billed concurrently with the related product sales, such as the sale of service-type warranties, and diagnostic and repair services. During the year ended December 31, 2025, parts and services revenue represented 97.5% of our consolidated revenue. Other revenue includes sales of scrap and other metals (including precious metals - platinum, palladium and rhodium - contained in recycled parts such as catalytic converters), bulk sales to mechanical manufacturers (including cores) and sales of aluminum ingots and sows from our furnace operations; all of which are typically acquired as byproducts of our salvage operations. Other revenue will vary from period to period based on fluctuations in commodity prices and the volume of materials sold. See Note 12, "Revenue Recognition" to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K for additional information related to our sources of revenue.

The preparation of the Consolidated Financial Statements in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP") requires management to make use of certain estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses, as well as related disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities in the Consolidated Financial Statements and accompanying notes. We base our estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that we believe are reasonable under the circumstances. Historically, we have not made significant changes to the methods for determining these estimates as our actual results have not differed materially from our estimates. We do not believe it is reasonably likely that the estimates and related assumptions will change materially in the foreseeable future; however, actual results could differ from those estimates under different assumptions, judgments or conditions.

Critical accounting estimates are those that are most important to the portrayal of our financial condition and results of operations, and which require us to make our most difficult and subjective judgments, often as a result of the need to make estimates of matters that are inherently uncertain. Based on this definition, we have identified the critical accounting estimates addressed below. For additional information related to significant accounting policies used in the preparation of our Consolidated Financial Statements, see Note 2, "Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" to the accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements.

Goodwill is obtained through business acquisitions and recorded at the estimated fair value at the date of acquisition. Goodwill is not amortized but instead tested for impairment annually or sooner if events indicate that an impairment may exist. Each of our segments is considered a separate reporting unit for purposes of testing goodwill. In performing this test, we compare the carrying value of the assets of our reporting units to its fair value. To estimate the fair value for our reporting units that carry goodwill, we use a weighted-average approach that is reviewed annually for changes in facts and circumstances. The weighting generally incorporates a 75% income approach via a discounted cash flow analysis and a 25% market approach via a guideline public company method. If the carrying value of these assets exceeds the estimated fair value, the asset is considered impaired and an impairment charge is recognized. In performing the test for impairment of goodwill, goodwill is allocated to the reporting units expected to benefit from the business combination.

paragraphs: LKQ Corporation ("LKQ," the "Company" or "we") 為全球車用產品經銷商，包括用於車輛維修與保養的替換零件、零組件及系統，以及提升車輛性能、功能與外觀的專業後市場產品與配件。
車用替換產品買家有選擇從主要四個來源購買的選項：由原廠製造商（"OEMs"）生產的新產品；由非原廠製造商生產的新產品，稱為後市場產品；從總損車輛中取得的回收產品；以及經過翻新或再製的再製品。我們 collectively 稱這三個非新 OEM 產品的來源為替代零件。

我們銷售多種替代性替換與維修零件，包括碰撞零件，這些通常是用於碰撞修復過程以恢復車輛外觀與安全的外觀零組件，例如 bumper covers、fenders、塗料與相關車體修復產品，以及燈具；硬體零件，這些通常是機械性質的內部零組件，例如發電機、起動馬達與離合器，或是作為例行維護更換的功能性零組件，例如剎車片、剎車盤與感測器、過濾器與電池；以及主要機械零件，例如引擎與變速箱。我們也銷售專業產品與配件，這些是用以提升車輛性能、功能與外觀的車用產品。
我們分為三個營運分部：北美（ formerly known as ("f/k/a") 批發 - 北美）；歐洲；以及專業產品，每個分部皆被列為應報告分部。請參閱財務報表附註 12，"收入確認" 以及附註 26，"分部與地理區域資訊"，以取得各應報告分部與各地理區域的財務資訊。

我們的北美分部為替代性車輛碰撞替換產品、塗料與相關車體修復產品，以及替代性車輛機械替換與維修產品的主要供應商，我們的銷售、處理與配送設施已覆蓋美國（"U.S."）與加拿大大多數主要市場。我們的歐洲分部為德國、英國（"U.K."）、比利時、荷蘭與盧森堡（Benelux 地區）、義大利、捷克共和國、奧地利、斯洛伐克、法國以及多個其他歐洲國家的替代性車輛替換與維修產品的主要供應商。我們的專業產品分部為專業車用後市場產品與配件的主要經銷商，覆蓋美國與加拿大大多數主要市場。
我們於 2025 年 9 月 30 日完成將 Self Service 分部出售給 Pacific Avenue Capital Partners, LLC 旗下公司的交易。我們已對前一時期的財務資訊進行重新歸類，以反映因出售 Self Service 分部而導致的已終止營運業務的財務資訊。請參閱財務報表附註 4，"已終止營運業務與資產處置"，以取得更多資訊。
我們的使命為成為全球車用零件與配件的領導性價值增加與可持續經銷商，透過提供給客戶最完整、可取得且成本效益最高的零件與服務解決方案，同時與我們所經營的社區與員工建立強大夥伴關係。為達成此使命，我們的策略聚焦於執行三大關鍵計畫：

我們致力於建立競爭優勢，擴大各營運分部的護城河，並維持我們在所經營市場的領導地位。我們專注於獲利性成長與提高自由現金流，同時維持一個強韌且具投資等級的資產負債表。我們培養一種創業精神與以員工為中心的文化，使我們的業務能靈活創新，並在所服務的市場中成功，其薪酬制度與我們追求長期總股東回報的策略相呼應。為持續提升我們資產組合的品質，我們的成長策略由內生性投資於自動化、生產力提升、人才發展與戰略收購所驅動，這些收購與車輛組合的持續演進相呼應。

本公司致力於透過推動各業務之運營卓越與精益管理，以產生可持續的投資回報。本公司持續評估並追求各種方案，以提升運營效率、增強毛利率，並善用各運營分部所存在的智慧財產權機會。透過針對性的生產力努力與嚴謹的成本管理方式，本公司目標特定的績效指標，包括自由現金流產生、內生成長與毛利率。本公司目前的方案包括優化營運資金、透過存貨最佳化方案提升毛利率，以及透過簡化營運據點與降低營運複雜度來降低銷售、一般及行政費用。

本公司專注於透過高效的資本配置策略，以最大化投資回報。本公司施以嚴格的標準，目標具有高協同效益的附加型收購，且與核心業務與策略相符。本公司積極處分不再符合本公司戰略願景、財務目標或具有限長期價值潛力的業務，如2024年處分波蘭、斯洛維尼亞與波斯尼亞的部分業務，以及2025年處分Self Service分部。此外，2025年，配合本公司持續簡化資產組合並專注於核心分部的策略，本公司已啟動評估潛在出售Specialty分部的程序。最後，本公司維持謹慎且嚴謹的財務政策，優先將現金回饋股東，透過股票回購與股息，同時維持投資等級的信用評等。
除上述內容外，於2026年1月26日，本公司董事會（"董事會"）宣佈已啟動一項全面評估戰略替代方案的程序，以提升股東價值。作為此評估的一部分，董事會正與其顧問合作，評估戰略替代方案，包括本公司可能出售的潛在方案。

為執行本公司交付獲利成長、推動精益運營模式並最大化投資回報的策略，本公司有時會進行重整與業務轉型方案。這些方案的範圍可從廣泛的改變，例如將非客戶面對的團隊集中化與標準化，以及處分非戰略性資產，到針對性的改變，例如合併閒置的設施與關閉績效不佳的據點。執行這些方案可能需要幾個月到幾年時間才能完全落實，視方案的範圍與複雜度而定。此外，這些方案可能根據執行過程所獲得的資訊而改變或擴展，當發現更多方案活動時亦可能增加。請參閱本年度報告10-K表單第II部第8項「合併財務資料」中第13項「重整與交易相關費用」，以取得與這些方案相關的重整費用之更多資訊。

本公司北美分部於美國、加拿大與墨西哥運營。在美國與加拿大，本公司主要透過本公司業務，包括Keystone與Bumper to Bumper（原為Canadian Automotive Group），銷售後市場、回收與重製的碰撞零件；後市場與回收硬體零件；以及回收與重製的主要機械零件。本公司亦在較小程度上提供車輛相關服務，包括移動與遠端診斷服務，以及混合動力電池重製與安裝服務，透過本公司業務，包括Elitek Vehicle Services與Green Bean Battery，以及其他業務。在墨西哥，本公司重製引擎與變速箱以供美國銷售。

本公司後市場產品包括常見於碰撞中易受損的項目，包括保險桿蓋、側板、塗料與相關車體修復產品，以及燈具，以及機械汽車零件與配件。本公司自有品牌產品包括以Keystone品牌行銷的Platinum Plus系列，以及為注重價值、常為自費消費者設計的"Value Line"產品類別。某些產品已獲得Certified Automotive Parts Association的認證，該組織為獨立機構，評估後市場零件的品質與性能，相對於原廠碰撞更換零件。本公司回收產品包括機械與碰撞零件，包括引擎；變速箱；門組；金屬板零件，如行李箱蓋、側板與引擎蓋；燈具；以及保險桿組裝件。

paragraphs: 下列有關我們財務狀況與營運成果之討論，應配合本公司經會計師核閱之合併財務報表及其附註，內容載於本年度10-K表報第II部，第8項「財務報表與補充資料」。有關2023年度項目及本公司財務狀況與營運成果之年對年變動比較，可參閱本公司2024年度10-K表報第II部，第7項「財務狀況與營運成果之管理層討論與分析」，該表報於2025年2月20日向SEC提交。除非另有說明或上下文另有要求，本「財務狀況與營運成果之管理層討論與分析」中所使用之「我們」、「我們」、「本公司」、「我們」、「LKQ」及類似詞彙，均指LKQ Corporation及其子公司。
我們是一家全球性車輛產品經銷商，包括用於車輛維修與保養之替換零件、零組件與系統，以及專門後市場產品與配件，用以提升車輛之性能、功能與外觀。
車輛替換產品買家有選擇從主要四個來源購買之選項：由OEM製造之新產品；由非OEM製造之新產品，稱為後市場產品；從總損車輛取得之廢件產品；以及經翻新或再製之再製品。我們 collectively 會將非OEM新產品之三個來源稱為替代零件。
我們分為三個營運部門：北美；歐洲；及專門業務，每個部門均作為應報告分部。我們已對前一時期財務資訊進行重新分類，以反映因出售Self Service部門而導致之停業業務之呈現。有關更多資訊，請參閱本年度10-K表報第II部，第8項「財務報表」附註4，「停業業務與資產處置」。

我們銷售多種替代性替換與維修零件，包括碰撞零件，通常為用於碰撞修復過程以恢復車輛外觀與安全之外部零組件，例如保險桿蓋、側板、塗料與相關車體修復產品及燈具；硬體零件，通常為內部零組件，為機械性質，例如發電機、起動馬達與離合器，或為例行維護中更換之功能性零組件，例如剎車片、剎車盤與感測器、過濾器與電池；以及主要機械零件，例如引擎與變速箱。我們亦銷售專門產品與配件，為用以提升車輛性能、功能與外觀之車輛產品。

我們之北美部門為替代性車輛碰撞替換產品、塗料與相關車體修復產品，以及替代性車輛機械替換與維修產品之主要供應商，銷售、處理與配送設施覆蓋美國與加拿大之大多數主要市場。我們之歐洲部門為德國、英國、比利時荷蘭地區、義大利、捷克共和國、奧地利、斯洛伐克法國及多個其他歐洲國家之替代性車輛替換與維修產品之主要供應商。我們之專門業務部門為專門車輛後市場產品與配件之主要經銷商，銷售覆蓋美國與加拿大之大多數主要市場。
我們之營運成果過去在每季與每年均有波動，未來亦可能持續出現波動，原因為多種因素，其中一些為我們所無法控制。請參閱上述特別聲明之前瞻性陳述與風險因素所提及之因素。由於這些因素及其他因素，可能目前為我們所不知，我們未來期間之營運成果可能出現波動。因此，我們之歷史營運成果可能無法反映未來表現。
我們持續管理與評估我們所擁有之業務與投資，以及我們所經營之市場。我們之收購策略為尋找具有顯著協同效益或關鍵能力之高獲利收購案。有關我們收購與投資之更多資訊，請參閱本年度10-K表報第II部，第8項「財務報表」附註3，「企業併購」及附註10，「權益法投資」。此外，我們有時會出售或處置與我們戰略願景、財務目標不符或長期價值潛力有限之業務。2025年，配合我們持續進行之策略，簡化資產組合並專注於我們
本公司核心分部，我們啟動了一項程序，探討出售我們專業分部的潛在可能性。請參閱本年度10-K申報書第二部分，第8項「合併財務報表」中第4項「已終止營運及資產處置」的附註，以取得更多有關我們資產處置的資訊。
除了上述內容外，於2026年1月26日，本公司董事會宣佈已啟動一項全面評估戰略選擇的程序，以提升股東價值。作為評估的一部分，董事會正與其顧問合作，評估我們的戰略選擇，包括本公司可能出售的潛在可能性。

我們將營業收入分為兩類：(i) 零組件與服務，以及 (ii) 其他。我們的零組件收入來自替代零組件與車輛產品的銷售，包括碰撞零組件，這些通常是用於碰撞修復過程的外觀與安全零組件；硬體零組件，這些通常是機械性質或功能性零組件，作為常規維護的一部分而更換；主要機械零組件；以及專業產品與配件，這些是用以提升車輛性能、功能與外觀的車輛產品。服務收入包括與相關產品銷售同時計費的附加服務，例如服務型保養合約的銷售，以及診斷與修復服務。在2025年12月31日結止的會計年度中，零組件與服務收入佔我們合併營業收入的97.5%。其他收入包括廢料與其他金屬（包括貴金屬－鉑金、鈀金與鈣金－含於回收零組件如催化轉換器中）的銷售、批量銷售給機械製造商（包括核心零件）以及我們熔爐運營所生產的鋁錠與鋁塊的銷售；這些通常為我們救災運營的副產品。其他收入會因商品價格波動與銷售材料的數量而有所變動。請參閱本年度10-K申報書第二部分，第8項「合併財務報表」中第12項「收入確認」的附註，以取得更多有關我們收入來源的資訊。

根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）編製合併財務報表，需要管理層使用某些估計與假設，這些估計與假設會影響所報告的資產、負債、收入與費用數額，以及相關的或有資產與負債披露。我們的估計基於歷史經驗與各種其他假設，我們認為在當前情況下這些假設是合理的。歷來，我們並未對這些估計的計算方法做出重大變更，因為我們的實際結果與估計並無重大差異。我們不認為在可預見的未來，這些估計與相關假設會有重大變更；然而，在不同的假設、判斷或條件下，實際結果可能與這些估計不同。
關鍵會計估計是指對財務狀況與營運結果的表現至關重要的估計，且需要我們做出最困難與主觀的判斷，通常因為需要估計本質上不確定的項目。根據這個定義，我們已識別出以下所討論的關鍵會計估計。如需更多有關編製合併財務報表所使用的重大會計政策資訊，請參閱本年度10-K申報書第二部分，第8項「合併財務報表」中第2項「重大會計政策摘要」的附註。

商譽是透過企業併購取得，並在取得日以預估的公平價值記錄。商譽不進行攤銷，而是每年進行減值測試，或在有跡象顯示可能減值時更早進行測試。我們的每個分部均被視為獨立的報告單位，以進行商譽的測試。在進行此測試時，我們比較報告單位資產的帳面價值與其公平價值。為估計報告單位中包含商譽的公平價值，我們使用加權平均方法，並每年根據事態與情況的變化進行審查。權重通常包含75%的收入方法，透過現金流折現分析，以及25%的市場方法，透過參考公開公司的指南方法。如果這些資產的帳面價值超過預估的公平價值，則認為該資產減值，並確認減值損失。在進行商譽減值測試時，商譽會分配至預期能從企業併購中受益的報告單位。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們面臨來自本地、國家、國際及基於互聯網的車輛產品供應商的競爭，這種競爭可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
我們依賴保險公司及客戶推廣替代零組件的使用。
與後市場產品相關的智慧財產權聲索可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
如果涉及事故或正在進行修理的車輛數量減少，或整體車輛人口中車輛類型的組成發生變化，我們的業務可能會受到影響。
商品價格的波動可能對我們的財務結果產生負面影響。
未來的公共衛生危機可能對我們的業務、營運成果、財務狀況及流動性產生重大負面影響，其性質與範圍極為不確定。
如果我們判定本公司 goodwill 或其他無形資產已發生減值，我們可能需對稅前收入產生重大費用。
本公司可能面臨產品責任索賠，並可能參與產品回收。
本公司可能無法成功取得企業或整合收購，且可能無法成功處置某些業務。
與本公司財務結構相關的風險
本公司負有相當程度的債務，這可能會對本公司財務狀況及未來取得融資能力與應對業務變動的能力產生重大不利影響。
本公司之信用協議及CAD Notes均對本公司及其子公司設有營運與財務限制，這可能會使本公司無法把握商業機會。
本公司可能無法產生足夠現金以償付所有債務，並可能被迫採取其他行動以履行債務義務，而這些行動可能無法成功。
本公司未來之資金需求可能需要本公司尋求重新融資債務或取得額外債務或權益融資，這些事件可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司之浮動利率債務使本公司面臨利率風險，這可能會導致本公司債務償付義務顯著增加。
本公司債務之償還取決於子公司的現金流。
本公司信用評等降級將對我們產生影響。
本公司股票回購及股息支付的金額與頻率可能有所變動。
法律與法規風險
本公司受環境法規所規範，並因環境相關事項產生成本。
本公司可能因全球氣候變遷所引發的法律、法規或市場反應而受到不利影響。
paragraphs: 下列風險因素及其他資訊包含於本年度報告表 10-K 中，應謹慎考量。上述任何風險或未知風險與不確定性之發生，可能對本公司之業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司之營運結果與財務狀況已受到北美、歐洲、臺灣及其他國家之經濟、政治與社會條件之影響，且可能持續受到影響，同時亦受到車輛所有者之經濟狀況及車輛銷售數量與類型之影響。
北美、歐洲、臺灣及其他本公司營運或營業所在地之經濟、政治與社會條件之變動，可能對本公司造成重大影響。因戰爭或戰爭威脅、限制性政府措施（例如關稅）、自然災害、核電設施事故、公共衛生緊急事件、重大物流中斷、制裁、公用設施中斷、恐怖主義與社會動盪等因素，可能導致供應鏈受損、營運成本上升、銷售與行銷活動受影響。

本公司亦受到多項其他因素之影響。例如，OEM 所生產與銷售之新車數量與類型，會影響本公司業務。道路上之車輛數量減少，可能導致維修需求減少。此外，本公司之銷售亦受到車輛所有者經濟狀況變動之影響。車輛所有者之經濟狀況受到多項因素影響，包括但不限於整體營商環境、利率、通貨膨脹、保險費率與免賠額、消費者負債水平、消費者信貸之可取得性、稅收、燃料價格、新舊車輛價格、失業率趨勢及其他影響消費者信心與支出之因素。許多這些因素均為本公司所無法控制。若通貨膨脹壓力或任何其他條件惡化，本公司之業務、營運結果、財務狀況與現金流可能受到不利影響。
此外，經濟條件，包括信貸取得困難，可能導致客戶、供應商、物流及其他服務提供者與金融機構之財務困難，進而導致重整、破產、清算及其他不利事件。這些對本公司業務夥伴之影響，可能對本公司之業務、營運結果、財務狀況與現金流造成不利影響。
本公司在烏克蘭有業務據點，並密切關注當地情況。此外，本公司部分供應商設立於中國與臺灣，因此若國際關係緊張或任何政治後果，可能對本公司之供應鏈造成影響。
